newsitem.title: CHINA: China stock indices end down on flagging sentiment.
newsitem.headline: China stock indices end down on flagging sentiment.

text.p: China stock indices ended down on Monday with sentiment flagging in the face of continued rumours about crackdown measures, this time predicting that 23 brokerages are to be punished for irregularities, brokers said.
Shenzhen B shares were also badly hit by news that the Shenzhen Development Bank had postponed its shareholders' meeting due to investigations into fluctuations in its share price, they said.
The Shanghai B index fell 0.249 points or 0.30 percent to 82.138 while the Shenzhen B index plummeted 6.85 points or 4.47 percent to 146.34.
Widespread rumours said the government is planning to punish 23 brokerages for contributing to trading volatility during market surges earlier this year, brokers said.
"The rumours about further clampdown measures are still in the market, which is greatly depressing market sentiment," one broker said.
Another broker said overseas investors who were seen buying on the Shanghai market during the surges early this year were now back on the sidelines.
"Domestic investors dominated the market with some institutions seen off-setting their positions while others took a wait-and-see attitude, resulting in today's dull trade," he said.
The Shenzhen Development Bank issued a statement in Monday's Shenzhen Securities Times on the postponement of its shareholers meeting but gave no details and bank officials declined to elaborate.
"The Shenzhen Bank's failure to conduct a shareholders' meeting sent bad vibes to the market," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
"Investors are very sensitive after many of the recent rumours concerning the market clampdown were proved to be true," an analyst at J&A Securities said.

The Shenzhen Bank's announcement had less effect on the domestic A share index, which pulled back from earlier heavy losses to end Monday down 1.48 points or 0.35 percent at 424.24 on turnover of 5.7 billion yuan, against Friday's 7.0 billion.
The B share market contains a larger proportion of Shenzhen-based companies compared with its A share counterpart, and was therefore harder hit, brokers said.
"Also, A share investors tend to take more risks and jumped in for bargain-hunting as soon as the Shenzhen bank shares steadied out," an analyst at a major domestic bank said.
Shenzhen Bank ended the day at 37.80 yuan, down 1.25 yuan or 3.2 percent, after hitting an intra-day low of 35.60 yuan.
On the Shanghai B share market, China First Pencil was the biggest loser on institutional unwinding selling, slipping $0.032 or 6.80 percent to $0.438 on volume of 447,700 shares.
Inner Mongolia Erdos Cashmere Products was the most actively traded on profit-taking, down $0.012 or 1.40 percent to $0.844 on volume of 1.3 million shares.

Shanghai's A index ended down 2.806 points or 0.21 percent to 1,307.821 points, but the SSE30 blue chip index bucked the market trend on institutional support buying, ending up 26.410 points or 0.68 percent to 3,908.338 points.
